competitive_conclusion: A real randomized active-versus-same-background signal for estimated fatigue-threshold workload merits retention. It does not show broad strength, independent living or pediatric/congenital benefit; small complete-case sample, formulation context and training-null counterevidence limit competitiveness. No automatic nominee replacement or cross-trial MVA efficacy order. No selective demand for MVA proof, which current nominees also lack.

studies.title: Oral nutritional supplement fortified with beta-alanine improves physical working capacity in older adults: a randomized, placebo-controlled study.

identity.background: Ensure High Protein, Abbott Nutrition: same batch for all arms, identical apart from beta-alanine addition. Each 8 liquid ounce serving (source also says227g) contains230kcal/12gprotein/31gcarbohydrate/6gfat.
identity.schedule: 800 or1200mg per serving, two servings/day for12weeks (84days); all arms consume ONS twice/day. These are studied exposures, not dosing advice.
identity.isolation: Randomized contrast isolates addition of beta-alanine on a common ONS background; not beta-alanine monotherapy against inert placebo or proof the background can be removed. No whole-product/retail reformulation equivalence.

studies.population: 60 older Central Florida volunteers,27men/33women, mean70.7±6.2y; no sarcopenia requirement established. Among44completers,68% structured activity≥twice/week and21% sedentary. Major recent surgery/asthma/uncontrolled cardiac or pulmonary disease/hypertension and exercise-interfering medications excluded. No disease-genotype/muscle-deficit model.
studies.design: Randomized after baseline; described double-blind/placebo-controlled. Allocation generation/concealment and blinding success not given. Normal exercise routines maintained, no assigned training program; diet advice aimed at isocaloric maintenance.
studies.missingness: 44/60 analyzed at follow-up; no ITT/imputation or missing-outcome sensitivity shown. One exclusion after creatine initiation, one sickness exclusion and other voluntary departures. Eight of21high-dose vs4of19low-dose vs4of20control lacked final measurements. Counts derived from randomized/completer totals; dropout reasons not fully mapped by arm.
studies.statistics: Treatment(3)×time(2)ANOVA; ANCOVA for baseline differences/follow-up interactions; Tukey post hoc pair comparisons and paired t-tests after main effects; alpha.05. No across-endpoint family correction, prespecified single primary endpoint/registry, exact pairwise CIs or sample-size effect assumption established. Stated target n≥12/arm for80%power based on earlier study.

PWCFT.definition: Submaximal discontinuous cycle ergometry with right-vastus-lateralis EMG. Starts30W,50rpm,two-minute stages, increments10–20W; EMG-slope significance threshold or75%age-predictedHR/RPE>13 stopping criteria; midpoint of significant/nonsignificant workloads or regression-based estimate when no slope threshold. Not directly measured sustained task duration, maximum force or unrestricted daily function.
PWCFT.between_contrast: Abstract explicitly reports both fortified-arm changes greater than ONS change,P<.05; main reports interaction and active gains. Exact pairwise P/adjustedmean/CI not supplied. High-v-lowP=.547.
limits: Percentages retained exactly as printed, not relabeled ordinary percent change of baseline group means; some do not equal that calculation and formula/individual basis is not specified.
Reported significance persists excluding paresthesia cases; no Ns or full sensitivity estimates, and this postrandomization exclusion does not establish blinding.
No familiarization. Test–retestICC.95 withSEM13.7W in10controlparticipants; alternate regression methodICC.95/SEM12.3W. Number requiring alternate estimator not reported.

STS.definition: Complete stands in30s, arms crossed; repetitions
STS.between_contrast: Baseline-adjusted high-v-lowP=.021; ONS-v-low not significant. High-v-ONS superior contrast not reported, so high-arm within improvement is not controlled efficacy against ONS.
STS.reliability: Control test–retest mean17.5→18.6,P=.026 despiteICC.96, consistent with a repeated-test change; source had no familiarization.

outcomes.grip: No significant treatment×time for dominant-handGRIPMAX orGRIPAVG; three3–5s maximal squeezes, nearestkg. No effect/CI supplied.

muscle_quality.definition: GRIPMAX(kg)/DEXA arm lean soft tissue mass(kg), not muscle histology or new absolute force
muscle_quality.between: After baseline adjustment high arm greater increase than low andONS,P<.05, Fig1caption; exact means/contrasts/CIs not available as numbers and native pixels not viewed.

outcomes.body_composition_diet: No significant bodyweight, lean/fat mass or dietaryprotein/totalcalorie changes reported. No general hypertrophy claim.

harms.paresthesia: ONS1200:2withdrawals+4continuing participants; ONS800:1continuing participant and no attributed withdrawal; not zero-harm or proven between-arm safety comparison. Potential sensory unblinding not assessed.
harms.laboratory: Pre/postCBC/chemistry measured in completers. Glucose remained above lab range; baselineMCHC below range. Authors report no measures newly outside range, but Table4 contains several nominal within-arm changes. No inference of long-term, pediatric or comprehensive safety equivalence.

studies.mechanism: Muscle carnosine was explicitly not measured; buffering/calcium-sensitivity explanations cite other work and are not mediation data. No BUB1B/BubR1-specific assay or checkpoint/fidelity endpoint reported in read scientific main. Beta-alanine does not inherit carnosine trial efficacy.
studies.funding: Abbott Nutrition grant; JRStout disclosed compensated presentations forAbbott; other authors declared no competing interests.
studies.reading: Complete scientific main text and allTable1–5text/Fig1caption read. No native pixels; no supplement/protocol/registry.

studies.title: Beta-Alanine Does Not Enhance the Effects of Resistance Training in Older Adults.
studies.reading: Complete original abstract, exact metadata, publisher acknowledgment/conflict excerpt only; main/PDF inaccessible.
studies.population: 27 randomized adults aged60–82 years; per-arm n, missingness and clinical eligibility unknown.
studies.intervention: 3.2g/day beta-alanine or placebo, with or without resistance training, for12 weeks. Publisher acknowledgment says NAI supplied sustained-release tablets and matching placebo. Tablet strength, excipients, adherence and harms not established.
studies.training: Three times weekly, two sets of15–25 repetitions on11 pneumatic machines, at50%1RM, alternating upper and lower body.
reported_outcomes: No significant group×time interactions for anthropometric/strength measures except leg-press1RM P=.010. Training groups improved P<.001, with no significant beta-alanine-attributable between-group difference.
No beta-alanine main effect or specified group×time interaction for20-repetition chest/leg-press tests. Some within-training power/fatigue comparisons were positive; these are not drug effects.
Authors report no beta-alanine effect on measures. This is a reported null within this small protocol, not equivalence or proof of no useful effects elsewhere.
studies.source_independence: Different authors/University ofMiami versus2013 UCF and a different design/dose. No shared cohort indicated in read material; no registry-based independence verification. Do not merge these as one cohort or claim confirmed independent replication.
studies.funding: NAI provided coded tablets at no cost; authors declare NAI had no role in design, collection, statistics or manuscript preparation.
unresolved: BUBR1 absence outside the abstract is not verified

identity_limits: Exact beta-alanine only. Do not join generic alanine, carnosine, beta-alanine salts/esters, preworkout combinations or unchanged Ensure product. NIH DSLD1061 exists but includes chemical derivatives; empty automatic aliases proposed unless integration explicitly preserves preparation scope.
optional_entry_justified: Yes, as a bounded functional reserve with explicit formulation/access/attrition/counterevidence limits. Independent source check and root admission remain separate. No automatic ledger count or nominee change.
source_reviewer_status: Bounded human functional reserve; partial native/access qualification

independent_precision_addendum.interpretation: Reliability limitation, not negation of the adjusted treatment contrast or evidence of absolute-force gain.
